title: A recording shows in history the moment you stop it
goal: User 2026-09-28: 'When I record video, now there seems to be a delay before it shows in history as if we're processing it more. I do not want processing to interfere with the speed of the experience.' Something now runs between stopping a recording and its history entry appearing. Measure before changing anything: time from Stop to the file closed, to the history tile, and list every piece of work that runs in that gap (thumbnail, frame reads, waveform, captions/transcription, loudness, metadata, a re-encode) and whether the tile waits on it.
acceptance: Reproduced first: record 5 s and 60 s clips with system audio and mic; log timestamps for Stop, file finalised, history tile shown, thumbnail shown; compare with the commit from before the delay (git bisect if needed) and name the commit that introduced it
The history tile appears within 300 ms of the file being finalised, with a placeholder thumbnail if its real one is not ready
Nothing optional runs before the tile appears: waveforms, thumbnails, frame reads and any analysis run afterwards at background priority and never block the history, the editor opening, or playback
No transcription runs unless the person asks for captions (see the on-demand captions task)
A drill or test measures Stop-to-tile and fails above 300 ms; a perf note in the commit

log.note: owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Reproduced with a probe drill (--recording-latency-diag, same stop-and-file sequence as RecordingCoordinator.stop before the fix): Stop to tile 21 ms (5 s, no sound), 61 ms (5 s, system+mic), 42 ms (60 s, no sound), 311 ms (60 s, system+mic), 820 ms (180 s, system+mic). Nearly all of it is SCRecordingOutput closing the file (outputFinished 15/60/38/310/818 ms); moving the file and listing it took 1-2 ms, and the poster/duration already ran lazily after the tile. No commit introduced it: ScreenRecorder is unchanged since 3c43f723 (2026-06-22). macOS spends about 4.5 ms per recorded second closing a file with sound, so the wait grew with longer recordings with sound.

Before building: a Premiere/QuickTime user expects Stop to be instant and the clip to be in the bin at once. Risks found and handled: (1) the saving tile has no file, so opening, copying, GIF, Show in Finder and paste all wait for it to land (CaptureStore.whenLanded); (2) deleting a saving tile trashes the file when it lands; (3) the folder listing spells the landed file differently (/private/var vs /var), which the first drill run caught (tile identity changed, poster never loaded), so the reserved URL is kept across the landing (reservedURLs); (4) a new recording started while the last one is still closing no longer has its stream cleared (ScreenRecorder.stop identity check).

Shipped: RecordingCoordinator.stop hides the stop control, lists the recording in history (CaptureStore.beginSaving) and fires the corner card at once, then files the file when macOS hands it back (finishSaving/failSaving). CaptureLibrary.merging (PhotonzCore, tested) folds saving recordings into the listing by date. After: Stop to tile 1-2 ms at 5, 60 and 180 s with system audio and mic; file lands 35-305 ms later; poster about 80 ms after that. Drill: Scripts/recording-latency-drill.sh <s> [--system-audio] [--with-microphone], exits 1 over RecordingStopBudget (300 ms). No transcription runs anywhere on the Stop-to-history path; auto-captions start only in an editor window (EditorState.writeCaptionsByThemselves), which the task captions-only-when-you-ask-for-them owns.

left rough: drill recordings run 4-7% longer than the time slept between start and stop (180 s slept, 192.5 s file). Picture and sound agree in the user's own recordings (ffprobe: 4.70 vs 4.73 s, 7.30 vs 7.32 s), so nothing a person would notice; not filed. Audit rough items (no picture of the saving tile; Copied-to-clipboard shows before the copy lands) stay here, not filed.

Stop now puts the recording in history and the corner card up at once (placeholder tile), and the file fills it in when macOS finishes closing it; open/copy/GIF/Show in Finder/clipboard wait for the file. Measured with the new probe drill Scripts/recording-latency-drill.sh: Stop to tile was 61/311/820 ms at 5/60/180 s with system audio + mic (all of it ScreenCaptureKit closing the file, no app commit caused it), now 1-2 ms at every length. Tests green (10,300), history and opening-a-recording walks pass. Commit 800a6d01; audit queue/audits/2026-09-28-recording-shows-in-history-at-stop.json.
